titolo: Lean community verifies Levent Alpöge's Riemann hypothesis proof
descr: Alpöge's 17‑million‑line Lean code proof of the Riemann hypothesis was confirmed correct by the Lean and Mathlib community on Nov 22 2026.
paragrafi: On 20 November 2026, Stanford mathematician Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann hypothesis written in the Lean proof assistant.
The proof consists of 17 million lines of Lean code that checks the argument automatically for errors.
The Lean and Mathlib community ran independent checks and reported the same result, stating they have full confidence in the proof’s correctness.
Verification tools used in Lean are designed so they cannot accept a flawed proof, and MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland listed the independent checks on his website.
The result arrived earlier than forecasts; Metaculus had expected a solution by May 2035, and Terence Tao had predicted a human‑AI collaboration around 2050.
perche: The verification shows how formal proof assistants can provide absolute certainty for complex mathematical results, reducing reliance on peer review alone. For AI users, it demonstrates a powerful use case for large language models like Claude in assisting formal mathematics, while free‑model enthusiasts can see the value of open tools that enable reproducible, community‑verified research.
